articles.content:
July 9, 2026

More intelligence from every token, stronger performance per dollar, and more capability on demand for your hardest work.

Learn about OpenAI’s latest model:

Update on August 21, 2026:OpenAI dropped the API and credit pricing of GPT‑5.6 Sol by over 20% for the next 3 months.

Update on July 30, 2026:OpenAI reduced the price of GPT‑5.6 Luna by 80% and GPT‑5.6 Terra by 20%.Learn more here.

We’re launching the GPT‑5.6 family of models for general availability following ourlimited preview⁠: our new flagship,Sol, alongsideTerra, a balanced model for everyday work, andLuna, our most cost-efficient model.

GPT‑5.6 Sol sets a new standard for both intelligence and efficiency, achieving state-of-the-art results across coding, knowledge work, cybersecurity, and science while outperforming previous and competing frontier models with fewer tokens and at lower estimated cost. The result is stronger performance per dollar: more successful work for the same spend, or comparable results at a lower total cost. We also introduce a new way to accelerate the most demanding work:ultrais our highest-capability setting, coordinating multiple agents across parallel workstreams to finish complex tasks faster. Stronger computer use and design judgment make GPT‑5.6 Sol our most polished collaborator yet, helping it inspect, refine, and deliver ready-to-use results.

We trained GPT‑5.6 to get more useful work from every token. OnAgents’ Last Exam⁠(opens in a new window), an evaluation of long-running professional workflows across 55 fields, GPT‑5.6 Sol sets a new high of 53.6, eclipsing Claude Fable 5 (adaptive reasoning) by 13.1 points. Even at medium reasoning, it beats Fable 5 by 11.4 points at roughly one-quarter the estimated cost. That efficiency extends to smaller models, which are essential to making intelligence more abundant and affordable: GPT‑5.6 Terra and GPT‑5.6 Luna outperform Fable 5 at around one-sixteenth the cost. On theArtificial Analysis Intelligence Index⁠(opens in a new window), a broad measure of intelligence spanning agentic work, coding, scientific reasoning, and general capabilities, GPT‑5.6 Sol with max reasoning comes within one point of Fable 5 while completing tasks in 61% less time at roughly half the estimated cost.

GPT‑5.6 launches with our most robust safeguards to date, designed to be resilient against determined and adaptive misuse without broadly limiting legitimate work. Before general availability, we put the models and safeguards through our most extensive evaluation period yet, combining human red teaming with large-scale automated testing. During the preview, we worked closely with expert organizations and with trusted partners to pressure-test defenses and strengthen safeguards before broader launch. The resulting system layers protections trained into the model with real-time checks, monitoring, and access calibrated to trust and risk.

GPT‑5.6 Sol is our best coding model yet. On theArtificial Analysis Coding Agent Index,GPT‑5.6 Sol with max reasoning sets a new state of the art at 80, 2.8 points above Fable 5, while using less than half the output tokens, taking less than half the time, and costing about one-third less. That advantage extends across the family: Terra performs just above Fable 5, while Luna outperforms Opus 4.8; each does so in roughly one-third of the time, with about half as many output tokens, and at approximately one-quarter the estimated cost. It also sets new state-of-the-art results on Terminal‑Bench 2.1 and DeepSWE, which test complex command-line workflows and long-horizon engineering in real codebases.

GPT‑5.6 can write and run lightweight programs that coordinate tools, process intermediate results, monitor progress, and choose the next action as work unfolds. This lets tool-heavy tasks advance with fewer tokens, fewer model round trips, and less guidance. Instead of requiring developers to script every step or passing every tool response back through the model,Programmatic Tool Calling⁠(opens in a new window)in the Responses API can filter large amounts of intermediate data, retain only what matters, and adapt its workflow along the way.

For problems that reward a greater investment of time and compute, GPT‑5.6 can push beyond this efficient default.maxgives GPT‑5.6 even more time thanxhighto reason and explore alternatives, run checks, and revise its approach.ultragoes further by coordinating four agents in parallel by default, trading higher token use for stronger results and faster time-to-result on demanding tasks. The charts below compare ultra’s default four-agent setup with a one-agent baseline across BrowseComp, SEC-Bench Pro, and Terminal-Bench 2.1; BrowseComp and SEC-Bench Pro also show 16-agent configurations. Across all three evaluations, adding parallel agents shifts the score-latency frontier upward and to the left, reaching stronger results in less time. In the API, developers can build ultra-like experiences using themulti-agent⁠(opens in a new window)beta in the Responses API.4,5,6

GPT‑5.6 delivers a step change in design judgment. With only high-level direction, GPT‑5.6 creates tasteful, ergonomic, and functional interfaces. Its stronger computer-use capabilities let it inspect and refine the rendered result—not just generate the underlying code or content—so it can catch visual and functional issues and apply finishing touches before handing the work back.

GPT‑5.6’s frontend capabilities also turn natural-language requests into polished, interactive explanations and visualizations within ChatGPT Work.

GPT‑5.6delivers better results for professional tasks. It takes messy context from your documents and everyday workflows like Slack, Notion, Microsoft 365, and Google Drive, and converts it into expert-level, shareable artifacts.

GPT‑5.6’s strength on knowledge work shows up in evaluations spanning long-horizon professional analysis, browsing, tool use, and computer use. GPT‑5.6 Sol sets new state-of-the-art results onBrowseCompat 92.2% andOSWorld 2.0at 62.6%; on OSWorld, it surpasses Opus 4.8 while using 85% fewer output tokens. Here, the performance-per-dollar gains extend across the GPT‑5.6 family. Luna nearly matches GPT‑5.5’s peak performance at less than half the estimated cost, while Terra surpasses it at a lower cost.

GPT‑5.6 Sol improves quality in presentations, documents, and spreadsheets,producing outputs that are more polished and accurate. It can create fully editable presentations from scratch, translating a prompt and source material into a coherent visual narrative with strong layouts, hierarchy, and design.

The improvement is especially pronounced when following templates and reference decks.GPT‑5.6 can infer a deck’s design system—layouts, typography, spacing, colors, and recurring content patterns, including rules embedded in the Slide Master—and apply those conventions consistently to new material. In this example, when asked to update numbers based on a reference file, the GPT‑5.5 output is missing key components from the master slide, while GPT‑5.6 follows the reference structure more faithfully.

GPT‑5.6 also creates more visually refined documents and spreadsheets. It follows complex reference formats more faithfully, which is important for repeatable knowledge work activities. It handles equations and financial models with greater precision, and makes better use of typography, spacing, hierarchy, and page or worksheet layout.

Early customers testing GPT‑5.6 saw improvements to knowledge work outputs across domains.

GPT‑5.6 is our strongest cybersecurity model yet, achieving frontier performance with significantly fewer tokens. OnExploitBench2,which measures progress from reaching vulnerable code through arbitrary code execution, it scores 73.5% versus GPT‑5.5’s 47.9% at a comparable output-token budget. OnExploitGym3,which asks agents to turn real-world vulnerabilities into working exploits, it almost doubles GPT‑5.5’s peak pass rate, from 15.1% to 24.9% under the two-hour cap; with six hours, it reaches 33.7%. OnSEC-Bench Pro,which tests proof-of-concept generation on complex software, it scores 71.2% versus GPT‑5.5’s 45.8% at an improved latency.1

GPT‑5.6 supports important defensive tasks such as secure code review, patching, threat modeling, and blue teaming. Qualified individuals and organizations inOpenAI Daybreak’s Trusted Access for Cyber⁠program can access more of its defensive capability through more precise safeguards for verified work in authorized environments, including vulnerability triage and validation, malware analysis, detection engineering, and patch validation.

Individuals canverify their identity and request trusted access⁠(opens in a new window), and organizations canapply⁠for their teams. Individual members will need to enableAdvanced Account Security⁠(opens in a new window)with hardware-backed passkeys by September 1 to retain access to our most cyber-capable frontier models; those who do not will return to default access. Users who do not already have hardware-backed passkeys can receivepreferred pricing⁠(opens in a new window)from our partner, Yubico. We are also taking additional steps to restrict access to high-risk entities and in high-risk jurisdictions.

GPT‑5.6 Sol also shows broad gains acrossscientific research. On life sciences evaluations, GPT‑5.6 demonstrates Pareto improvements over GPT‑5.5 on real-world biology, life science research workflows, and chemistry.

GPT‑5.6 is our strongest model yet for accelerating AI research. Inside OpenAI, researchers use it across the development loop: diagnosing failures, optimizing training systems, running experiments, and interpreting results. We already saw that acceleration and stronger adoption during the internal testing period of GPT‑5.6, as average daily output tokens per active researcher were more than twice the highest level observed for GPT‑5.5.

articles.title: Google Launches Gemini Decisions API With Gemini Decision 1 at $0.10/M Tokens
articles.content: Google has launched the Gemini Decisions API, powered by a new model, Gemini Decision 1 (gemini-decision-1). The Gemini Decisions API does not generate text. It scores up to 1,000 typed questions against one shared input and returns calibrated probabilities. For developers, this targets the small branching calls inside agents: routing, policy checks, tool selection and grading. Google prices it at $0.10 per 1M input tokens, with zero output tokens billed. TL;DR Size: Context is 262,144 tokens (256K) across shared input and all questions. Runs on: Google-hosted API only (Gemini Developer API, v1beta). No open weights or self-hosting. Performance: Leads 7 of 9 accuracy benchmarks in Google’s table, with the lowest calibration error. Best: 92.2% on JevBench (public split). Worst: 58.7% Macro-F1 on Amazon ESCI, its lowest score. It also trails Jev 1.14 on When2Call (79.9% vs 82.0%). Bottom line: Best: multimodal, calibrated decisions in 150-250 ms. Worst: not the cheapest; Jev 1.14 costs $0.68 vs $0.88 on the shared suite. What is the Gemini Decisions API? Gemini Decision 1 is a specialized multimodal model from Google built for closed-set decisions. It reads text, images, video, audio and PDFs in one prefill pass. Output token usage is always 0. Your code branches directly on the returned numbers. Each request has 3 parts: a model ID, a shared input, and a map of questions. The docs define 3 question types: noul (yes/no): returns the probability of yes, bounded between 0.01 and 0.99. choice: picks 1 of 2 to 255 options and returns normalized probabilities for every option. score: rates input on 2 to 255 ordered rubric levels and returns a probability-weighted score. Every answer carries a confidence value from 0 to 1. Google suggests routing low-confidence cases to a fallback or a human reviewer. Questions are scored in parallel and cannot see each other. How does Gemini Decision 1 work? Standard models decode an answer token by token, then your code parses it. Gemini Decision 1 instead scores your candidate options in one forward pass. Google reports median model compute of 50-100 ms and 150-250 ms end to end. That holds for inputs up to 16K tokens and stays nearly flat from 1 to 100 questions. Billing follows the same design. The shared input is billed once per request, however many questions you ask. Each question adds only its own instruction and criteria tokens. There are no thinking-token, transcription or OCR charges. && Gemini Decision 1 benchmarks Google tested Gemini Decision 1 against 3 rivals. They are TypeSafe Jev 1.14, GPT-6 Luna on OpenAI Decisions and Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite. All figures below are self-reported by Google. Refusals and safety blocks count as incorrect. A no-cost tier is available for prototyping in Google AI Studio. Python, JavaScript and REST guides are in the documentation. Ecosystem support is rolling out across OpenRouter, LangChain, Vercel AI SDK, LiteLLM, Pydantic AI, Pipecat, LiveKit and OpenCode. Support in Gemini on Google Cloud is listed as coming soon. Google already uses it internally. Gemini Notebook routes queries to model tiers with it, serving everyday queries with up to 40% lower latency. articles.title: Google DeepMind Releases AlphaGenome 2 for Cell-Type-Specific Variant Effects
articles.content: Google DeepMind has released AlphaGenome 2, a DNA model that predicts variant effects in specific cell types. AlphaGenome 2 is a conditional sequence-to-function model. It reads 1 Mb of DNA plus a target cell state. Its predecessor averaged across bulk tissues. The new model resolves closely related cell types and adapts to unseen single-cell datasets without fine-tuning. It is available through the AlphaGenome API for non-commercial research. TL;DR Size: Input is a 1 Mb (1,048,576 bp) DNA window, human or mouse. Runs on: Hosted API only for now. Training used 2048 TPU v4 chips; weights come “upon final publication”. Performance: Beats fine-tuned AlphaGenome 1, Borzoi and Scooby on single-cell eQTL and enhancer-gene benchmarks. Best: 43% recall at 90% sign accuracy on TenK10K sc-eQTLs, versus 23% for AlphaGenome 1 fine-tuned. Worst: Outside accessible chromatin, sign prediction AUROC reaches only 0.63. Bottom line: Best: cell-state conditioning from raw scRNA-seq. Worst: no local weights, non-commercial only. What is AlphaGenome 2? AlphaGenome 2 is a U-Net style model with a convolutional encoder, an 11-block transformer and a decoder. AlphaGenome 1 predicted a fixed catalog of thousands of tracks in parallel. AlphaGenome 2 instead predicts outputs for 1 condition per call. The condition is a 256-dimensional embedding. It modulates activations through FiLM layers in the encoder, transformer and decoder. Conditioning only the decoder or output layers gave minimal gains. Conditioning the encoder and transformer drove most of the improvement. Outputs cover RNA coverage, CAGE, splicing, chromatin accessibility, histone marks, TF binding and contact maps. CpG methylation is new. How was AlphaGenome 2 trained? Training runs in 4 stages: Pre-training across bulk data plus 3,977 single-cell RNA and ATAC pseudobulk tracks from 36 studies. Condition refinement, which tunes only the embeddings and FiLM layers. Distillation of 8 teacher models into 1 student, using mutated input sequences. Post-training that maps a single-cell expression encoder into the frozen model’s condition space. That encoder was trained on over 100 million human scRNA-seq profiles, largely from CELLxGENE. Researchers can pass raw counts and get a condition embedding. The docs allow up to 256 cells per call. How does AlphaGenome 2 perform on benchmarks? On GTEx tissues, median Pearson r for cross-tissue expression changes rose from 0.61 to 0.71. Within tissues, explained cell-type variance rose from 23% to 34% for scRNA-seq. The main result is on TenK10K single-cell eQTLs across 28 immune cell types. At 90% precision, AlphaGenome 2 recovered 30% of causal variants. AlphaGenome 1 fine-tuned on single-cell data recovered 16%. Direction-of-effect recall rose from 23% to 43%. On held-out ENCODE-rE2G CRISPRi data, enhancer-gene AUPRC reached 0.78. AlphaGenome 1 scored 0.73, a Borzoi ensemble 0.61. The gap was widest for enhancers 100 to 2,500 kb away: 0.62 versus 0.48. For assay imputation, AlphaGenome 2 beat the Avocado baseline on 166 of 181 held-out tracks. On an unseen Parkinson’s cohort, it reached 41% recall versus 17% for cohort-tuned Scooby. & How does it compare with other DNA sequence models? What can developers access today? AlphaGenome 2 and Colab tutorials are live through the API. An API key is free for non-commercial use. Commercial research is in private preview. The alphagenome Python package exposes the model under alphagenome.models.v2. DeepMind also released precomputed atlases. One covers enhancer-gene links across 640 primary cell conditions. Another scores about 7 million common and GWAS variants across 510 conditions. Both are on the downloads page. Key Takeaways AlphaGenome 2 conditions a 1 Mb DNA model on 1 cell type per call. Causal sc-eQTL recall at 90% precision rose from 16% to 30%. Raw scRNA-seq counts can define new cell states without retraining. Precomputed scores cover about 7 million variants across 510 conditions. Access is API-only and non-commercial for now. Check out the paper, the DeepMind blog, the API docs and the GitHub repo. articles.title: MBZUAI’s IFM Releases PAN 2, an Open 29B World Model for Physical AI
articles.content: The Institute of Foundation Models (IFM) at MBZUAI released PAN 2, an open world model for physical intelligence. The PAN 2 world model takes a scene and a text action and simulates the outcome as video. IFM announced it on X on November 10, 2026. Weights, training code and inference code ship under Apache 2.0. For robotics and agent developers, the pitch is simple: test a plan in simulation before acting on it. TL;DR Size: 29B-parameter diffusion transformer (MMDiT), dense. Inputs: text plus an optional first frame. Output: 704×1248 video at 24 fps, up to 20 s. Runs on: Data-center GPUs. Each worker holds the full 29B model in BF16, with block offloading as fallback. Performance: Leads 6 tested models on full plans. Trails MiniMax-H3 on single actions and human preference. Best: 34.0% full-plan completion on 100 multi-step tasks, the highest of all models tested (self-reported). Worst: About 2 in 3 plans miss a step. Physics-IQ system default: 37.48 vs 42.91 for MiniMax-H3. Bottom line: Best: a fully open world model that leads on multi-step plans. Worst: long plans still fail often, and hardware needs are high. What is PAN 2? PAN 2 is a general-purpose world model from IFM that simulates how a scene changes after an action. It follows the Generative Latent Prediction (GLP) architecture from IFM’s Critique of World Models paper. It succeeds PAN, released in November 2025. The goal is simulative reasoning. An agent proposes plans, PAN 2 simulates each one, and the agent acts on the best. How does PAN 2 work? PAN 2 splits simulation into 2 kinds of reasoning: Conceptual reasoning: An LLM reads the observation and the requested actions. It writes the next world state as structured JSON: events, timed actions bound to actors, and camera motion. Any instruction-following LLM can fill this role. IFM’s report uses Kimi K3 by default. Perceptual reasoning: A 29B MMDiT predicts the video latents. IFM trained it from scratch on hundreds of millions of annotated videos. A frozen Qwen3.5-9B text encoder conditions it. The Wan 2.2 VAE decoder renders the final frames. IFM’s ablation shows the LLM matters. With no conceptual reasoning, full-plan completion drops from 34.0% to 0.0%. Step completion falls from 75.1% to 8.7%. A format-only rewrite recovers part of the gap, reaching 27.8% full-plan completion. IFM also dropped gameplay, animation and simulation footage after early training. A 9B test model trained without it won 58% of blinded votes. articles.title: KT·마이크로소프트, 네트워크 문제 감지하는 AI 에이전트 개발…장애 탐지 10분에서 2~3분으로 단축
articles.content:
KT와 마이크로소프트가 숙련된 통신망 엔지니어의 경험과 전문지식을 학습한 에이전틱 인공지능(AI) 플랫폼을 공동 개발해 네트워크 장애 탐지 시간을 기존 10분 이상에서 2~3분으로 단축했다. AI가 통신망의 이상 징후를 실시간으로 분석하고 장애 원인을 신속하게 파악하도록 지원하면서, 네트워크 운영의 효율성과 안정성을 동시에 높이는 성과를 거뒀다.

마이크로소프트는 11일(현지시간) KT와 공동 개발한 지능형 네트워크 운영 플랫폼 'AIO-Net'의 기술 구조와 현장 적용 성과를 공개했다. 이 플랫폼은 전국 통신망에서 발생하는 방대한 데이터를 AI 에이전트가 지속적으로 분석하고, 숙련 엔지니어의 피드백을 반영해 판단 능력을 개선하는 방식으로 운영된다.

KT에 따르면 AIO-Net은 네트워크 이상을 탐지하는 시간을 2~3분으로 줄였으며, AI 에이전트가 장애를 조사하고 원인을 분석해 보고서를 작성하는 데 걸리는 시간도 평균 5분으로 단축했다. 이는 기존 수작업 방식보다 약 50% 감소한 수준이다.

이동통신 가입자 약 2,900만 명을 보유한 KT는 모바일과 인터넷, TV, 전화 등 다양한 통신 서비스를 운영하고 있다. 통신망이 복잡해지면서 장비에서 발생하는 경고와 이상 신호를 분석하는 업무도 증가하고 있어, 장애를 조기에 발견하고 고객 서비스에 미치는 영향을 신속하게 판단하는 것이 중요한 과제로 떠올랐다.

숙련 엔지니어의 노하우 학습...AI가 매분 통신망 이상 분석

AIO-Net의 핵심은 KT가 '마이스터(Meister)'로 인정한 숙련 네트워크 엔지니어들의 현장 경험을 AI 에이전트의 판단 과정에 반영한 것이다.

기존 네트워크 운영은 장애 경고가 발생하면 담당자가 여러 시스템에 분산된 데이터를 확인하고 원인을 추적해야 했다. AIO-Net은 이러한 정보를 하나의 화면에 통합하고, AI가 이상 징후와 관련 데이터를 분석해 운영자가 신속하게 대응 방안을 결정하도록 지원한다.

플랫폼은 마이크로소프트 애저(Microsoft Azure)를 기반으로 구축됐으며, 마이크로소프트 파운드리(Microsoft Foundry)의 여러 거대언어모델(LLM)을 활용한 AI 에이전트가 전국 네트워크 장비에서 생성되는 데이터를 매분 분석한다.

특히 KT의 표준운영절차(SOP)와 숙련 엔지니어들이 20년 이상 현장에서 축적한 경험을 활용해 장애 원인을 판단하도록 설계됐다. AI가 분석한 결과와 판단 과정은 기록되며, 현장 엔지니어가 이를 검토하고 평가한 내용은 향후 유사한 장애나 새로운 유형의 이상 상황을 분석하는 데 활용된다.

이러한 지속적 개선 방식은 AI 분야에서 '힐 클라이밍(hill-climbing)'으로 불리는 반복적 최적화 접근과 연결된다. 초기 모델의 성능에만 의존하지 않고 실제 운영 과정에서 수집되는 피드백을 통해 판단 품질을 높이는 구조다.

KT 네트워크 엔지니어 오희영 마이스터는 "원인을 파악하는 시간이 크게 줄면서 어떻게 대응할지 판단하고 필요한 조치를 취하는 데 더 집중할 수 있게 됐다"며 "무엇보다 고객 서비스에 영향이 있는지를 판단하는 시간이 훨씬 짧아졌다"고 설명했다.

AI는 분석과 근거 제시까지만...장비 제어 권한은 제한

이번 플랫폼의 또 다른 특징은 AI 에이전트의 자율적 판단 기능과 실제 통신망 제어 권한을 명확하게 분리했다는 점이다.

AIO-Net은 네트워크 이상을 탐지하고 장비 상태를 조회하며 장애 원인을 분석해 대응 방안을 제안할 수 있지만, 실제 장비에 명령을 내려 조치하는 권한은 갖지 않는다. 최종 판단과 실행은 네트워크 운영자가 담당한다.

이를 위해 AI 에이전트가 사용할 수 있는 명령을 사전에 승인된 조회 전용 명령으로 제한했다. 이러한 제약은 단순히 AI에 지시하는 프롬프트 수준이 아니라 애플리케이션 자체에 적용돼, AI가 허용되지 않은 명령을 시도하더라도 실행할 수 없도록 설계됐다.

이는 AI의 잘못된 판단이나 명령이 실제 통신망 장애로 이어질 수 있는 위험을 차단하기 위한 조치다. 통신망처럼 안정성과 신뢰성이 중요한 핵심 인프라에서는 AI의 분석 능력을 활용하되 사람에게 최종 통제권을 유지하는 '휴먼 인 더 루프(Human-in-the-loop)' 방식이 중요하다는 점을 보여준다.

정선일 KT 네트워크운용혁신본부장은 "운영의 효율화보다 망 안정성이 최우선의 가치"라며 "AI의 권한은 분석과 근거 제시까지이며, 최종 판단과 조치는 사람이 한다"고 강조했다.

마이크로소프트 엔지니어 현장 투입...핵심 장비 280대로 확대

AIO-Net은 기존의 외부 개발 용역 방식과 달리 KT 개발팀과 마이크로소프트의 현장 밀착형 엔지니어(FDE)가 공동으로 설계하고 구현했다. 마이크로소프트 엔지니어들은 KT 사무실에서 개발팀과 함께 코드를 작성하고, 운영자의 피드백을 수집·반영하거나 필요할 경우 변경 사항을 이전 상태로 복원하는 절차까지 공동 구축했다.

이호송 KT AIO-Net 개발팀장은 AI 기술이 빠르게 발전하는 환경에서는 기존의 외주 개발 방식만으로 대응하기 어렵다며, 마이크로소프트 개발진이 현장 문제를 함께 정의하고 구현 과정에 참여한 점을 협력의 주요 성과로 평가했다.

현장 운영자의 참여 방식도 달라졌다. 과거에는 별도로 피드백을 요청해야 했지만, 현재는 운영자가 플랫폼을 사용하는 과정에서 평가 정보가 자연스럽게 축적돼 AI 시스템의 지속적인 개선에 활용된다.

KT는 현재 핵심 네트워크 장비 70대에 적용된 AIO-Net을 280대로 확대하고, 향후 가입자와 더 가까운 액세스망까지 적용 범위를 넓힐 계획이다.

이번 사례는 에이전틱 AI가 기업의 반복적인 정보 처리 업무를 넘어 실제 통신 인프라의 운영과 장애 대응 과정에 적용되고 있음을 보여준다. 특히 숙련 인력의 전문지식을 AI에 반영하고, AI가 제시한 분석 결과를 사람이 검증하는 구조는 통신뿐 아니라 전력망과 데이터센터 등 안정성이 중요한 산업 인프라에도 참고할 만한 접근 방식이다.

한편, 마이크로소프트는 이번 KT와의 공동 개발 사례를 이날 공식 뉴스룸에 소개했다. KT는 AI를 통한 반복적인 장애 분석 업무의 부담을 줄이고, 네트워크 운영 인력이 통신 시설 관리와 서비스 품질 개선 등 보다 중요한 업무에 집중할 수 있도록 플랫폼을 지속적으로 고도화할 계획이다.
articles.summary: KT와 마이크로소프트는 숙련 엔지니어의 경험과 표준운영절차를 반영한 네트워크 운영 에이전트 플랫폼 AIO-Net을 공동 개발했다. Azure와 Microsoft Foundry의 여러 LLM을 활용해 전국 장비 데이터를 매분 분석하며, KT에 따르면 이상 탐지 시간을 기존 10분 이상에서 2~3분으로 줄였다. 장애 조사·원인 분석·보고서 작성도 평균 5분으로 단축됐고, 판단 기록과 엔지니어 검토를 후속 분석에 활용한다. 에이전트에는 애플리케이션 수준에서 조회 전용 명령만 허용하고 실제 장비 제어는 운영자가 맡도록 해, 핵심 인프라에서 분석 자동화와 실행 권한을 분리했다.

We are releasing GPT‑5.5 with our strongest set of safeguards to date, designed to reduce misuse while preserving access for beneficial work. articles.title: Fish Audio Releases Live 3, a Full-Duplex Voice Model That Reacts in 186 ms
articles.content: Fish Audio has released Live 3, a full-duplex voice model built for real-time voice agents. The Fish Audio Live 3 full-duplex voice model keeps listening while it speaks. That lets a caller pause, say “mm-hmm,” or change their mind without breaking the call. For developers, the pitch is simple. Turn-taking moves out of hand-tuned pipeline rules and into the speech model. TL;DR Product: A full-duplex voice model built for real-time voice agents Runs on: Hosted Fish Agent Platform and Fish Audio API; on-premises for enterprises. Performance: Fish Audio shows behavior demos, but publishes no benchmark scores. Best: Can decide to respond in as little as 186 ms for short reactions like “mm-hmm.” What is Fish Audio Live 3? Live 3 is a full-duplex voice model from Fish Audio that listens and speaks at the same time. The core argument is that speed and timing are different problems. An agent can reply fast and still speak at the wrong moment. A pause after “What time do you open?” usually ends a turn. A pause in the middle of a phone number does not. How does Live 3 handle turn-taking? Most voice agents split recognition, reasoning, speech generation and turn-taking across separate pipeline stages. Fish Audio team states that Live 3 moves conversational timing into the speech model. It was trained on real human conversations to learn when to acknowledge, wait, respond or stop. They framed the old approach as piling on “more rules and more thresholds.” Fish Audio instead wants the model to learn timing from data. A separate reasoning layer still holds the agent’s instructions and tools. The Fish Audio team walks through 3 behaviors: Acknowledging without taking over. A caller reads “415… 555… 0132.” Live 3 may say “okay, 415” between chunks, then wait. Telling a backchannel from an interruption. A caller saying “yeah” lets the agent continue. “Wait, actually, I just need Thursday” makes it stop. Waiting through corrections. For “two pizzas… no, three,” Live 3 waits instead of logging the wrong order. How fast is Live 3? Fish Audio states Live 3 can decide to respond in as little as 186 ms. That figure covers short reactions such as “mm-hmm,” “okay” and quick confirmations. The full answer is prepared in parallel. This is a floor for small reactions, not time-to-first-audio for a complete reply. Fish Audio has not published a latency distribution. Third-party tracker OrcaRouter also reports no Artificial Analysis score for Live 3 as of November 11. & How do developers deploy Live 3? Live 3 is available on the Fish Agent Platform, through the Fish Audio API, and on-premises for enterprises. The Agents platform is in public beta. Agents expose a REST surface under /v1/agent/*. Browser sessions run through @fishaudio/agent-client or @fishaudio/agent-react. Agents can answer phone numbers, connect over WebRTC, or sit in a website widget. The Live 3 page lists 2,000,000+ library voices, including cloned voices. A pending docs pull request shows Live 3 enabled with voice.engine: "live3". With it on, speech recognition is fixed to fish_audio:transcribe-stream-1. Fish Audio’s current docs say that model also classifies overlaps as interruptions or acknowledgements. How much does Live 3 cost? The Live 3 page lists $0.035 per minute, down 50% from $0.07, until December 31, 2026. It says the plan includes Live 3. The pricing docs say the $0.07 list rate covers STT, TTS, basic LLMs, knowledge retrieval and tool calls. Phone calls add $0.01 per minute. A number costs $1.20 per month. New accounts get a $5 trial balance. How does Live 3 compare with other full-duplex voice models? articles.title: ADIndex: Layer-Adaptive Sparse Attention Indexing via Group-Level Distillation
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12956v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA) reduces the computational cost of attention through token-level selection. However, its indexer still scores the entire causal prefix for each query, making indexing a dominant source of latency in long-context inference. Notably, the indexer alone can account for more than 50% of total prefill GPU time at long context lengths. To address this bottleneck, we propose ADIndex, an Adaptive and Distillation-driven Indexing method for token-level sparse attention. ADIndex integrates three key components: (i) a layer-wise calibration strategy that adaptively accommodates cross-query retrieval overlap, motivated by our observation of pronounced inter-layer heterogeneity; (ii) a group-level distillation scheme that leverages this heterogeneity to efficiently train adaptive layer-wise group indexers, capturing salient retrieval signals from individual queries; and (iii) a low-latency inference strategy that reduces repeated full-prefix scans through token bank sharing within query groups while retaining query-specific refinement. Experiments on DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.1 demonstrate that ADIndex preserves near-lossless task performance on LongBench, LongBench v2, and RULER while delivering substantial efficiency gains over standard DSA, including prefill and decoding kernel speedups of up to 6.22x and 3.40x, respectively, at a context length of 256K across the layer-wise reuse configurations, as well as an end-to-end serving speedup of 1.54x at a context length of 128K.
articles.summary: ADIndex는 DeepSeek Sparse Attention에서 긴 문맥 전체를 반복 탐색하는 인덱서의 병목을 줄이는 방법이다. 계층별 검색 중복도를 보정하고 그룹 단위 증류와 토큰 뱅크 공유를 결합하면서, 개별 질의에 대한 정밀화는 유지한다. DeepSeek-V3.2와 GLM-5.1 실험에서 장문 벤치마크 성능을 거의 유지하며 256K 문맥에서 프리필·디코딩 커널을 각각 최대 6.22배·3.40배 가속했다고 보고했다. 128K 문맥의 전체 서빙 가속은 1.54배로, 커널 개선과 실제 서비스 수준의 효과를 구분해 볼 필요가 있다.

articles.title: Agent Architecture Cost-Success Trade-offs: A Controlled Evaluation across Enterprise-Style SOPs
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12953v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Enterprises increasingly use large language model agents to execute standard operating procedures (SOPs): long, branching, tool-intensive workflows. Yet there is little controlled evidence for choosing among competing agentic architectures. Holding the model, tasks, and tools fixed and varying only the architecture, we compare four designs (a function-calling single agent, a skill-augmented agent, centralized multi-agent orchestration, and a triage swarm; eight arms) across 13 enterprise SOPs, and introduce a skill-definition quality rubric to build matched high and low-quality skill corpora. Three takeaways emerge. (1)~\textbf{There is no universal best architecture; the right choice is SOP-dependent.} On a given SOP, task success ranges from under $10\%$ on the hardest to near $100\%$ on the easiest; no architecture is statistically separable in aggregate, and added structure only plausibly pays off on complex, branching SOPs (a directional, not yet significant, trend). (2)~\textbf{Added architecture cost must be justified by a task-success gain.} Every coordinated arm (multi-agent or skill-augmented) spends $1.4$--$4.7\times$ the tokens and $2.6$--$5.8\times$ the latency of the single agent for gains that are usually small and rarely significant, making the single agent the efficient default; high-quality skills do lift success (to $73.1\%$ from $67.4\%$) while degraded skills fall below it. (3)~\textbf{Implementation quality outweighs the single- versus multi-agent choice.} A plausible multi-agent implementation loses to the single agent, yet a targeted redesign of it becomes the only arm to significantly beat the baseline ($75.6\%$ vs.\ $67.4\%$).

articles.title: DrugCoding: A Scientific Programming Agent for Drug Discovery
articles.content: Drug discovery involves multiple interconnected research stages, including molecular design, property prediction, and virtual screening. These processes are characterized by complex workflows, interdependent computational tasks, and diverse specialized tools, placing substantial demands on the coordination of scientific models and computational resources. However, existing large language model (LLM)-based scientific agents still face challenges in autonomous planning of complex tasks, adaptive selection of specialized models, and reliable execution of multi-stage scientific computations, limiting their effectiveness in automating complex drug discovery workflows. To address these challenges, we propose DrugCoding, a scientific programming agent system that integrates scientific task planning, adaptive model routing, multi-agent collaboration, and programmatic tool execution. DrugCoding enables autonomous task planning and dynamic model adaptation for complex research objectives. It can flexibly invoke specialized scientific models, autonomously generate and execute code according to task requirements, and leverage multi-agent collaboration to support efficient execution and reliable validation of complex scientific tasks. To evaluate DrugCoding's performance in scientific tool invocation and multi-stage task execution, we conduct multi-turn tool-calling experiments across diverse language models and scientific tool interfaces. Experimental results demonstrate that DrugCoding achieves an average session-level Pass@1 of 97.35% on the full benchmark, outperforming the strongest baseline, Codex, by 9.24%. On the challenging subset, DrugCoding achieves 97.92%, exceeding the strongest baseline.
articles.summary: DrugCoding은 신약 탐색의 분자 설계·물성 예측·가상 스크리닝을 지원하기 위해 과학 작업 계획, 전문 모델 라우팅, 멀티에이전트 협업과 코드 실행을 통합한 시스템이다. 연구 목표에 맞춰 전문 모델을 선택하고 코드를 생성·실행하며 다단계 계산의 검증을 지원한다. 연구진은 다중 턴 도구 호출 벤치마크에서 평균 세션 단위 Pass@1 97.35%를 보고하며 가장 강한 기준선인 Codex보다 높은 결과를 제시했다. 이는 과학 도구 활용과 워크플로 실행 성능에 관한 결과로, 실제 신약 발견이나 임상 성과를 입증한 것은 아니다.

articles.title: Embodied Science Agents: Making Embodied Experimental Design Learnable
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12958v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent advances in large models have accelerated AI for Science toward agentic science, where AI agents autonomously conduct scientific discovery. Realising this vision requires closing the loop between computational reasoning and physical experimentation, positioning self-driving laboratories (SDLs) as critical enablers. However, existing SDLs exhibit a fundamental paradox: foundation model integration has increased linguistic sophistication while severing physical grounding. By treating models as disembodied planners that output symbolic workflows for separate robotic systems, current architectures inherently block the development of embodied experimental intuition. We argue that overcoming this paradox requires embedding \emph{learnability} along three interdependent axes: cognitive learnability (learning what to investigate), experimental learnability (learning where to search), and embodied learnability (learning how to act). Building on this view, we introduce the Embodied Science Agent (ESA), which unifies digital intelligence with physical embodiment through three synergistic components: a Digital Agent that provides cognitive and experimental learnability via memory-based reasoning and Bayesian optimisation, an Embodied Agent that provides embodied learnability via generalisable instrument control, and an Embodied Unified Interface for seamless coordination. We validated ESA in autonomous wastewater treatment experiments, navigating over 200 million possible conditions. Through 15 continuous rounds, ESA raised the final solution transmittance from 82\% to 99.7\%, corresponding to a 98.5\% reduction in residual dye concentration and near-complete decolourisation, while its learned visuomotor policies generalised across varying instrument placements, a promising step toward next-generation SDLs for autonomous scientific discovery.
articles.summary: Embodied Science Agent는 기억 기반 추론·베이지안 최적화를 수행하는 디지털 에이전트와 일반화 가능한 기기 제어를 담당하는 체화 에이전트를 통합했다. 언어 모델의 실험 계획과 실제 장비 조작을 분리하는 대신 무엇을 탐구하고 어디를 탐색하며 어떻게 행동할지 함께 학습하는 구성을 제안한다. 폐수 처리 실험에서는 2억 개 이상의 가능한 조건을 탐색 대상으로 삼아 15회 연속 실험으로 최종 용액 투과율을 82%에서 99.7%로 높였으며, 잔류 염료 농도는 98.5% 감소했다고 보고했다. 학습된 시각·운동 정책은 기기 배치 변화에도 일반화됐지만, 다른 실험 분야에서도 같은 성과를 낼지는 추가 검증이 필요하다.

articles.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
articles.content: External memory enables LLM agents to improve from experience by distilling trajectories of past tasks into concise lessons for new tasks. However, memory can also lead to memory-induced degradation, where an agent fails on tasks it would solve without memory, often because it follows a lesson that is incorrect, or misapplies or misreads a valid one. This is because lessons are inferred from trajectories labeled only with task success or failure, yet are typically provided without the trajectories they came from, leaving the agent no way to check them. To address this, we introduce WikiTrace, an evidence-linked memory system designed to let agents check each lesson against its original trajectory. Specifically, motivated by the finding that a trajectory often still holds the evidence needed to catch an erroneous lesson, WikiTrace stores each lesson as a concise insight linked to a summary of why its trajectory succeeded or failed and to the raw trajectory itself. Then, on a new task, the agent starts from all insights and, whenever one lacks details needed to act, conflicts with another, or comes from a failed task, descends through its links with terminal tools to fill in missing details or correct the insight before acting. We validate WikiTrace on five agentic benchmarks, showing that it consistently outperforms existing memory approaches and a baseline given the same insights alone, while also reducing memory-induced degradation. Our code is available at https://github.com/yukyeongleee/wikitrace
articles.summary: WikiTrace는 에이전트가 과거 경험에서 얻은 교훈을 원래 실행 기록과 연결해 검증할 수 있도록 하는 외부 기억 시스템이다. 간결한 통찰, 성공·실패 이유 요약, 원본 궤적을 계층적으로 연결하고 정보 부족이나 충돌이 발생하면 도구를 통해 근거를 확인하게 한다. 연구진은 5개 에이전트 벤치마크에서 기존 기억 방식과 같은 통찰만 제공한 기준선보다 일관되게 높은 성능을 보였다고 보고했다. 잘못되거나 부적절하게 적용된 기억 때문에 원래 풀 수 있던 작업에 실패하는 현상을 줄였으며, 구현 코드도 공개했다.

articles.title: Seeing Is Not Believing: Counterfactual Lesion Erasure Teaches a Small Medical Vision-Language Agent to Report Only What the Image Shows
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.13006v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) often report a finding because the question names it; standard benchmarks miss this. From public segmentation datasets we build counterfactual views without manual annotation: the lesion erased by inpainting, a same-shape control edit elsewhere, and unedited lesion-free images. The evidence sensitivity gap (ESG) is the rate of absent-or-refer answers after erasure minus the rate after the control edit; it is zero for a model that ignores the image or reacts to both edits alike. MedScope-4B (Qwen3.5-4B, LoRA, image tools) was trained on label-derived trajectories, selected by a pre-registered rule and tested once against nine frontier and six open VLMs; four pre-registered checks then probed the mechanism. On 507 internal cases across five imaging types, MedScope-4B reached ESG 0.758 and claimed an erased lesion in 9.6% of cases, against 0.27-0.47 and 41-62% for the frontier models (all p<0.001), without significant loss of accuracy on real lesions. Without counterfactual views ESG fell to 0.279+-0.107 (three seeds); the effect replicated on MedGemma 1.5 4B and two unseen inpainting tools. At four external centres the advantage held but frontier models detected more real lesions; on a fresh external test MedScope-4B detected 0 of 48 pneumothorax films, with net utility below gemini-4-argon's (-0.36 [-0.50, -0.23]). Matching the control edit was not shown to matter; over three seeds no fresh-external ESG advantage over removal-based DPO was established; a paired-view consistency objective did not beat a matched-compute control, while that continuation alone cut erased-lesion claims on unseen tools at every seed, at a cost in sensitivity at one. Training on erased and edited images gives a small model an evidence-gated disposition that prompting does not give frontier models; it does not improve perception, and rare critical findings need coverage.
articles.summary: MedScope-4B 연구는 병변을 지운 영상과 대조 편집 영상을 학습에 활용해, 질문에 언급됐다는 이유만으로 병변을 보고하는 의료 VLM의 오류를 줄이고자 했다. 내부 507건 평가에서 지워진 병변을 있다고 주장한 비율은 9.6%로 비교 프런티어 모델의 41~62%보다 낮았고, 실제 병변 정확도의 유의한 손실은 관찰되지 않았다. 그러나 별도의 신규 외부 평가에서는 기흉 영상 48건을 모두 놓쳤으며, 외부 기관 평가에서도 프런티어 모델이 실제 병변을 더 많이 탐지했다. 영상 근거에 따라 답변을 제한하는 학습과 실제 지각 능력 향상은 별개이며, 환각 감소만으로 임상적 유용성을 판단해서는 안 된다는 결과다.

articles.title: SepsisFlow: an event-stream foundation model for continuous risk warning and trajectory modelling in ICU sepsis
articles.content: Sepsis is a leading cause of ICU death with heterogeneous onset and course, yet most warning models predict only whether sepsis will occur, leaving clinicians uncertain of its onset context and early trajectory once an alarm sounds. To answer these questions on one hourly clock from ICU admission, we built SepsisFlow: before onset, it combines a Mamba model pretrained on 2.57 million EHRs with about 1,700 hourly features in gradient-boosted trees to predict 6/12/24-h risk; at onset, it fuses Mamba and tabular encoders via a gated network into continuous patient states defining onset contexts; after onset, it encodes 72-h organ-support and physiological trajectories via an attention bidirectional recurrent network into early courses. For pre-onset warning in MIMIC-IV, SepsisFlow detected more cases than NEWS2, qSOFA, and SIRS at equal alarms, gaining about 8 cases per 100 from hourly updating, while outperforming 16 retrained algorithms and maintaining risk ranking in eICU. At onset, its contexts separated 2% cardiovascular-ICU from 15%-17% other 28-day mortality, and within each context after onset, persistent support carried fivefold higher mortality than de-escalation. SepsisFlow establishes a foundation-model paradigm for continuous risk and trajectory stratification in critical care.
articles.summary: SepsisFlow는 중환자실 입원 이후 패혈증 발생 전 위험, 발생 시점의 상태, 발생 후 경과를 시간 단위로 연결하는 시스템이다. 257만 건의 전자의무기록으로 사전학습한 Mamba와 약 1,700개 시간별 특징을 활용하는 그래디언트 부스팅 모델을 결합해 6·12·24시간 위험을 예측한다. MIMIC-IV에서는 같은 경보량에서 기존 임상 점수보다 더 많은 사례를 탐지했고, 시간별 갱신으로 100건당 약 8건의 추가 탐지 이득을 보고했으며 eICU에서도 위험 순위화 성능을 유지했다. 발생 후 장기 지원·생리 궤적까지 구분한다는 점이 특징이지만, 제공된 결과는 실제 도입에 따른 사망률 개선을 입증하지는 않는다.

articles.title: Pulse or Provenance? What rPPG-Based Deepfake Detectors Learn
articles.content: Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) has been proposed as a physiological cue for deepfake detection, based on the premise that synthesized faces lack a genuine cardiac signal. We examine what rPPG-style detectors learn on Celeb-DF++ (22 forgery methods) and FaceForensics++ (FF++), using one identically sampled window per real and fake video. On talking-face forgeries, simple chrominance traces reach an AUC of 0.998, exceeding a dedicated rPPG extractor (0.87). Controlled experiments indicate that this signal is not physiological in origin. On fully synthesized forgeries, it is equally discriminative when extracted from background regions or from full frames without face detection, and it is concentrated above the 0.7 to 4 Hz heart-rate band. It is largely removed by shuffling frame order but persists after normalizing resolution, frame rate and encoding, and an independent reimplementation reproduces these findings. Removing high-frequency content makes most synthesized videos appear real, adding it makes real videos appear fake, and injecting a synthetic pulse has little effect. In controlled self-reenactment experiments with two generators, animating a face from a single frame introduces the same high-frequency signal, whereas reconstructing each frame from its own source does not. Face-based chrominance detectors trained on Celeb-DF++ classify over 99% of real FF++ videos as fake, indicating that they largely encode video source rather than manipulation, and a CLIP-based detector exhibits the same behavior. A frozen CLIP backbone matches or exceeds fusions of CLIP with rPPG and frequency features. Finally, we show that the official Celeb-DF and Celeb-DF++ splits share identities and source-video content between training and test, and that custom protocols reusing test videos and identities in training inflate weaker detectors by up to 0.30 AUC.
articles.summary: 이 연구는 얼굴 영상의 원격 광용적맥파를 이용한다는 딥페이크 탐지기가 실제로는 심박보다 영상 출처와 생성 과정의 신호를 학습할 수 있음을 보였다. 일부 합성 영상에서 높은 판별력을 보인 색차 신호는 얼굴이 아닌 배경에서도 나타났고, 심박 대역보다 높은 주파수에 집중됐다. Celeb-DF++로 학습한 탐지기가 실제 FF++ 영상의 99% 이상을 가짜로 분류했으며, 공식 데이터 분할에서도 인물과 원본 영상 내용의 중복을 발견했다. 실무적으로는 높은 내부 AUC만 믿기보다 출처가 다른 데이터와 누출을 통제한 평가로 탐지기의 일반화 능력을 검증해야 한다는 경고다.

articles.title: BuySideFlow: A Point-in-Time Benchmark for LLM Agents in Investment Research
articles.content:
arXiv:2611.12966v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate SQL and SQL--Python workflows for investment research, but ensuring point-in-time (PIT) validity remains challenging. Agents must enforce disclosure cutoffs and select the appropriate historical states and record versions throughout data retrieval and financial analysis. We introduce \textsc{BuySideFlow}, a benchmark of 408 practitioner-derived Chinese-language tasks spanning equities, funds, fixed income, and macroeconomics over a fixed snapshot from a licensed production financial database. We provide executable references and a taxonomy of temporal errors, pairing result checks with expert audits of executed workflows. We evaluate nine agent configurations on all tasks, with result accuracy ranging from 16.2\% to 36.8\%. An audit of 900 runs on 100 shared tasks confirms PIT violations in 193 of the 380 runs that pass result checks (50.8\%), showing that output agreement alone does not establish temporal validity.
articles.summary: BuySideFlow는 투자 분석 에이전트가 당시 공개돼 있던 정보만 사용했는지 평가하는 시점 정합성 벤치마크다. 실제 운영 금융 데이터베이스의 고정 스냅샷을 바탕으로 주식·펀드·채권·거시경제를 아우르는 중국어 실무 과제 408개와 실행 가능한 정답 기준을 구성했다. 9개 에이전트 구성의 결과 정확도는 16.2~36.8%였고, 별도 감사에서 결과 검사를 통과한 380회 실행 중 193회가 시점 정합성을 위반했다. 정답 숫자가 맞더라도 미래 정보나 잘못된 기록 버전을 사용했을 수 있어, 금융 에이전트 검증에는 데이터 조회와 실행 경로 감사가 필요함을 보여준다.

articles.title: 검수도 답변도 호출도 AI가? 커머스API의 2026
articles.content: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ ​ 발표 내용 같은 API 스펙이 AI 에게 검수되고, 문의 답변의 근거가 되고, tool 로 호출되기까지 — 커머스API 플랫폼이 올해 진행한 AI native 과제 세 건의 설계 결정과 운영 결과를 소개합니다. ​ 발표 대상 API 를 만들거나 운영하는 백엔드 개발자 게이트웨이·플랫폼 운영자 LLM·MCP 를 서비스에 연결하려는 개발자 ​ 목차 도입 : 우리가 맡은 플랫폼과 AI 로 할 수 있게 된 것 1장. 라우팅 룰 AI 검수 - 자동화 규칙 50개를 데이터로 만들고, 판단이 필요한 규칙까지 자동으로 검수하는 엔진 2장. articles.summary: 네이버는 커머스API의 같은 명세를 AI 검수, 문의 답변 근거, 에이전트 도구 호출에 활용하는 세 가지 실무 과제를 소개했다. 라우팅 룰 검수에서는 자동화 규칙 50개를 데이터화하고 판단이 필요한 규칙까지 검사하는 엔진을 다루며, MCP 게이트웨이에서는 API 명세를 에이전트 도구로 변환하면서 기존 검수·통제를 적용한다. 기술지원 영역에서는 흩어진 지식을 정리해 AI용 문서와 답변 지원으로 연결하는 과정을 공유한다. 정량 성과는 제공된 소개문에 없지만, 기존 API 운영 체계를 유지하면서 에이전트 연동을 확장하려는 개발팀에 참고할 만한 사례다.

articles.content: 네이버 사내 기술 교류 행사인 NAVER Engineering Day 10th 에서 발표되었던 세션을 공개합니다. ​ ​ 발표 내용 AI변화와 함께 성장하는 디자인시스템을 소개합니다. ​ AI 산출물이 프로덕션으로 이어지지 못하는 5가지 이유 스펙·HTML·이미지 어떤 입력이든 Figma로 모으는 전략과, Figma를 중심에 둔 이유 AI와 설계자가 같은 블록으로 조립하도록 컴포넌트·디자인 토큰·design.md로 설계 의도를 표현하는 방법 접근성·인터랙션·엣지 케이스가 담긴 코드 컴포넌트와 Code Connect로 Figma와 코드를 잇는 방법 이미지 → Figma, Figma → 마크업, Figma ↔ 마크업 비교 데모 (Claude Code 플러그인 defign-toolkit) Figma의 높은 자유도를 보완하는 deFign assistant 도입 후 달라진 점과 앞으로의 방향 (Spec → Code) ​ 발표 대상 AI로 만든 결과물을 실제 서비스로 옮기는 데 드는 재작업이 고민인 기획자·디자이너·개발자 디자인시스템을 AI 시대에 맞게 확장하려는 팀 기존 R&R과 프로세스를 유지하면서 AI 도입 효과를 높이고 싶은 조직 ​ 목차 문제 제기: 왜 지금 디자인시스템인가? 현실: AI 산출물은 왜 프로덕션이 되지 못하나 접근: 프로세스 안에서 단계 사이를 자동화 넘어야 했던 고민 3가지 고민 1. 의도를 표현할 어휘가 필요하다 고민 2. 설계 의도와 기술 이슈는 어떻게 처리할 것인가? 고민 3. Figma와 컴포넌트는 어떻게 연결할 것인가? 우리가 제공하는 것 정리: 그래서 얻은 것 앞으로 ​ ​ ◎ NAVER Engineering Day란? ​ NAVER에서는 사내 개발 경험과 기술 트렌드를 교류를 할 수 있는 프로그램이 많이 있습니다. 그중 이제는 매회 평균 100개 이상의 발표가 이루어지는 NAVER Engineering Day를 빼놓을 수 없는데요. 2016년부터 시작된 ENGINEERING DAY는 실무에서의 기술 개발 경험과 새로운 기술과 플랫폼 도입 시 유용하게 활용될 수 있는 팁 등을 공유하며 서로 배우고 성장하는 네이버의 대표적인 사내 개발자 행사입니다.(관련 포스팅 보기) 올해 진행된 NAVER Engineering Day의 일부 세션을 공개합니다. ​ [동영상 제공 채널 안내] 네이버 TV 서비스 종료로 인해 기존 네이버 TV 채널을 클립(@devrel_d2)으로 이동하였습니다. 앞으로도 많은 관심과 팔로우 부탁드리겠습니다.
articles.summary: 네이버는 AI가 생성한 결과물을 실제 서비스에 적용하기 위해 Figma 중심 디자인시스템과 코드 컴포넌트를 연결하는 접근을 소개했다. 컴포넌트와 디자인 토큰으로 설계 의도를 표현하고, 접근성·인터랙션·예외 상황을 담은 코드 컴포넌트를 Code Connect로 Figma와 잇는 방식이다. 이미지와 Figma, 마크업 사이의 변환·비교 데모 및 설계 보조 도구 사례를 통해 기존 프로세스의 단계 간 자동화를 다룬다. 제공된 소개문에는 정량적인 생산성 개선치가 없지만, AI 산출물의 재작업을 줄이기 위한 공통 설계 어휘와 검증 체계의 중요성을 보여준다.

articles.title: Transparency Disclosures for Chain-of-Thought Monitorability
articles.content: Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring is one of the most valuable tools for monitoring advanced AI systems, but it is under threat. We argue that frontier AI developers should report specific indicators to make these threats trackable and to better facilitate coordination to preserve CoT monitorability. We identify five indicators that are both highly relevant and reasonably feasible to disclose, one for each link in a five-step chain on which CoT monitoring depends. The first, third-party CoT access and base architecture specifications, also underpins external verification of the rest. The others span CoT quality (naturalness and faithfulness) and monitoring effectiveness (detection and uplift). An audit of current disclosures by Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google DeepMind shows that no developer covers the full set, but that every indicator has been reported by at least one frontier developer. Because current disclosures rely largely on developers' own evaluations, we also recommend that a cross-developer audit be repeated with deeper access than public disclosures allow, either by embedded evaluators working within developers or by an Independent Verification Organization.
articles.summary: 이 연구는 고도화된 AI의 추론 과정 모니터링을 유지하기 위해 프런티어 개발사가 공개해야 할 다섯 가지 지표를 제안했다. 제3자의 추론 과정 접근과 기본 아키텍처 정보, 추론의 자연스러움·충실성, 모니터링의 탐지 성능과 추가 효과를 연결해 평가하는 틀이다. Anthropic·OpenAI·Google DeepMind의 공개 내용을 감사한 결과 모든 지표를 다루는 개발사는 없었지만, 각 지표는 적어도 한 개발사가 보고한 사례가 있었다. 연구진은 자체 평가 공개만으로는 충분하지 않다며 내부 접근이 가능한 평가자나 독립 검증 조직을 통한 교차 감사를 권고했다.
